title: Second commandment (CCC 2142–2159)
hook: the holy name, and your own name too

segments.voice: Yesterday, the first commandment: faith, hope and love aimed at God, and no luck charm in his place. Your line was god first.

The coffee shop is loud. The barista slides a cup across the counter and calls out a name that's almost yours, spelled the way no one has ever spelled it. Later that week, at a funeral, a grandson reads his grandmother's full name aloud, every part of it, slowly, and the room goes still. Same thing, a name: in one place scribbled and forgotten, in the other held like something precious. Today's commandment is about a name, God's, and it ends up being about yours.
screen: `A NAME MISSPELLED ON A CUP.` → `A FULL NAME READ AT A FUNERAL.` → `GOD'S NAME, AND YOURS.`

segments.voice: In the Douay-Rheims: "Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain." The Catechism begins with a gift: God entrusts his name to those who believe in him, as he told Moses his name at the burning bush. To give someone your name is to let them call on you. So the commandment asks for the respect you'd give the name of someone you love. Then it names what goes against it. Blasphemy: words of hatred or contempt aimed at God, the Church or the saints. Using God's name to cover crimes, or to justify violence against a people. Careless swearing, where the holiest name becomes filler. And a false oath: calling on God as witness to a lie. Jesus goes further in the Sermon on the Mount: don't swear at all; let your yes mean yes. The Church still allows an oath for a serious and just reason, like testimony in court. A person is baptized in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and receives their own name in the Church. God calls each one by name, the Catechism says, and everyone's name is sacred: the icon of the person, a sign of the dignity of the one who bears it. In Revelation, the one who overcomes is promised a white stone with a new name on it, known only to the one who receives it. So the second commandment guards two names at once: the name above every name, and the one on your coffee cup.
screen: `GOD ENTRUSTS HIS NAME.` · `NOT IN VAIN: BLASPHEMY, FALSE OATHS.` · `GOD CALLS EACH ONE BY NAME.` · `A WHITE STONE, A NEW NAME.`

segments.voice: If you pray, say God's name once, slowly, the way you'd say the name of someone you trust, and let the silence after it be long; if you don't, say the name of someone you love just as slowly, and notice how a name carries a whole person. Then say your own name, quietly, as though someone kind were saying it to you.
Second commandment. Thou shalt not take the name of the Lord thy God in vain: respect for God's name, and, the Catechism adds, for every person's name. Today's word.
Your line: names are holy. God's name first, and then every other name after it. That's the day.

howItsDone: Catholics are taught to speak God's name with reverence; at baptism a child receives a Christian name, which may be a saint's, and the priest baptizes in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

fork.setup: you're asked to swear before God that something is true, and it's a small lie that would spare everyone trouble. what does the second commandment say?
options: never call God to witness a lie.
fork.reveal: the Catechism says a false oath calls on God to be witness to a lie, and calls perjury a grave lack of respect for the Lord of all speech.

trapdoor: what you thought: don't curse using God's name.
what it means: respect God's name, keep your oaths true, and honor every person's name as sacred.
what a scholar hears: God entrusting his name at the bush, the Catechism's 'icon of the person', and the white stone of Revelation 2:17.

the home as a little church

chat.says: Is the commandment about God's name just about not swearing?
options: It's wider: no blasphemy or false oaths, and the Catechism adds that every person's name is sacred.
Yes, it bans curse words only; using God's name to back up a lie falls under another rule.
It's about choosing a saint's name at baptism; swearing belongs to a different commandment.
chat.meaning: The Catechism names blasphemy, careless swearing and false oaths, then turns to us: everyone's name is sacred, the icon of the person.

blasphemy.meaning: words of hatred or contempt aimed at God

Sermon on the Mount.meaning: Jesus' long teaching in Matthew chapters 5 to 7

Revelation.meaning: the last book of the Bible

icon.meaning: an image; here, a sign standing for the whole person

notes: CCC 2142–2159 paraphrased (copyrighted translation). 'Icon of the person' follows CCC 2158; 'everyone's name is sacred' follows CCC 2158; oath for a serious and just reason follows CCC 2154.
'Using God's name to cover crimes, or to justify violence against a people' paraphrases CCC 2148; confirm wording.
Fork reveal follows CCC 2151 (a false oath calls on God to be witness to a lie) and CCC 2152 (perjury is a grave lack of respect for the Lord of all speech); confirm.
Exodus 20:7 quoted from Douay-Rheims; confirm exact wording.
Isaiah 43:1 ('called thee by thy name') deliberately not quoted; CCC 2158 cites it and a Keeper may wish to add it in Douay-Rheims.
howItsDone: 'which may be a saint's'; CCC 2156 says the name can be a saint's. Confirm phrasing.
